sanskrit: atīva hṛṣṭāḥ śvasṛgālavāyasā; baḍāḥ suparṇāś ca vṛkās tarakṣavaḥ vayāṃsy asṛkpāny atha rakṣasāṃ gaṇāḥ; piśācasaṃghāś ca sudāruṇā raṇe
english: Exceedingly glad were the dogs, jackals, and crows, the herons and great birds, the wolves and hyenas, the carrion fowl that drink blood, the hosts of rākṣasas, and the fearsome bands of piśācas upon that battlefield.

sanskrit: tvaco vinirbhidya piban vasām asṛk; tathaiva majjāṃ piśitāni cāśnuvan vapāṃ vilumpanti hasanti gānti ca; prakarṣamāṇāḥ kuṇapāny anekaśaḥ
english: Tearing through the skin they drank the fat and the blood, and likewise devoured the marrow and the flesh; they ripped away the entrails, laughing and singing as they dragged off the corpses, many at a time.

sanskrit: śarīrasaṃghāṭavahā asṛgjalā; rathoḍupā kuñjaraśailasaṃkaṭā manuṣyaśīrṣopalamāṃsakardamā; praviddhanānāvidhaśastramālinī
english: It bore along masses of bodies, its water was blood, chariots were its rafts, hemmed in by elephants like crags; men's heads were its stones, flesh its mire, and it was garlanded with scattered weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: mahābhayā vaitaraṇīva dustarā; pravartitā yodhavarais tadā nadī uvāha madhyena raṇājiraṃ bhṛśaṃ; bhayāvahā jīvamṛtapravāhinī
english: Set flowing then by the foremost warriors, a river dreadful and uncrossable as the Vaitaraṇī coursed mightily through the midst of the battlefield, terrifying, carrying along the living and the dead.

sanskrit: pibanti cāśnanti ca yatra durdṛśāḥ; piśācasaṃghā vividhāḥ subhairavāḥ sunanditāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ bhayaṃkarāḥ; samānabhakṣāḥ śvasṛgālapakṣiṇaḥ
english: There the hideous, manifold, most frightful bands of piśācas drank and feasted, rejoicing greatly, terrible to all that breathe, sharing their feast alike with dogs, jackals, and birds.

sanskrit: tathā tad āyodhanam ugradarśanaṃ; niśāmukhe pitṛpatirāṣṭrasaṃnibham nirīkṣamāṇāḥ śanakair jahur narāḥ; samutthitāruṇḍakulopasaṃkulam
english: That battlefield, grim to behold at the onset of night, resembling the realm of the lord of the dead, thronged with risen ghosts and heaps of headless trunks—gazing upon it, the men slowly withdrew.

sanskrit: apetavidhvastamahārhabhūṣaṇaṃ; nipātitaṃ śakrasamaṃ mahāratham raṇe 'bhimanyuṃ dadṛśus tadā janā; vyapoḍhahavyaṃ sadasīva pāvakam
english: Then the people beheld Abhimanyu, that great chariot-warrior equal to Śakra, cast down in battle, his precious ornaments fallen away and shattered—like a sacrificial fire in the assembly from which the oblation has been borne off.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmiṃs tu nihate vīre saubhadre rathayūthape vimuktarathasaṃnāhāḥ sarve nikṣiptakārmukāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When that hero, the son of Subhadrā, leader of chariot-bands, had been slain, all the warriors loosened their chariot-armor and laid down their bows.

sanskrit: upopaviṣṭā rājānaṃ parivārya yudhiṣṭhiram tad eva duḥkhaṃ dhyāyantaḥ saubhadragatamānasāḥ
english: They sat down, encircling King Yudhiṣṭhira, brooding upon that one grief alone, their minds fixed upon the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ abhimanyau hate vīre bhrātuḥ putre mahārathe
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, sore stricken with grief, lamented, now that the hero Abhimanyu, his brother's son, that great chariot-warrior, was slain:

sanskrit: droṇānīkam asaṃbādhaṃ mama priyacikīrṣayā bhittvā vyūhaṃ praviṣṭo 'sau gomadhyam iva kesarī
english: Wishing to do me a kindness, he broke through the impenetrable host of Droṇa and entered the battle-array, like a lion into the midst of a herd of cattle.

sanskrit: yasya śūrā maheṣvāsāḥ pratyanīkagatā raṇe prabhagnā vinivartante kṛtāstrā yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: Before him the brave great archers who faced him in the hostile ranks, accomplished in arms and mad for war, were broken and turned back.

sanskrit: atyantaśatrur asmākaṃ yena duḥśāsanaḥ śaraiḥ kṣipraṃ hy abhimukhaḥ saṃkye visaṃjño vimukhīkṛtaḥ
english: By his arrows Duḥśāsana, our bitterest foe, though he stood to face him in battle, was swiftly stunned and driven to flight.

sanskrit: sa tīrtvā dustaraṃ vīro droṇānīkamahārṇavam prāpya dauḥśāsaniṃ kārṣṇir yāto vaivasvatakṣayam
english: Having crossed the unfordable great ocean that was Droṇa's host, that hero, the son of Kṛṣṇā, reached Duḥśāsana's son and then went to the abode of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: kathaṃ drakṣyāmi kaunteyaṃ saubhadre nihate 'rjunam subhadrāṃ vā mahābhāgāṃ priyaṃ putram apaśyatīm
english: How shall I look upon Arjuna, son of Kuntī, now that the son of Subhadrā is slain? Or upon the illustrious Subhadrā, who shall not see her beloved son?

sanskrit: kiṃ svid vayam apetārtham aśliṣṭam asamañjasam tāv ubhau prativakṣyāmo hṛṣīkeśadhanaṃjayau
english: What senseless, incoherent, unfitting words shall we two speak in answer to them both, to Hṛṣīkeśa and to Dhanaṃjaya?

sanskrit: aham eva subhadrāyāḥ keśavārjunayor api priyakāmo jayākāṅkṣī kṛtavān idam apriyam
english: It is I alone who, wishing to please Subhadrā and Keśava and Arjuna, longing for victory, have wrought this grievous wrong.

sanskrit: na lubdho budhyate doṣān mohāl lobhaḥ pravartate madhu lipsur hi nāpaśyaṃ prapātam idam īdṛśam
english: The greedy man perceives not the faults of his act; from delusion greed arises. Coveting the honey, I did not see this precipice before me.

sanskrit: yo hi bhojye puraskāryo yāneṣu śayaneṣu ca bhūṣaṇeṣu ca so 'smābhir bālo yudhi puraskṛtaḥ
english: He who should have been set first at the feast, in carriages, on couches, and in adornments—him, a mere boy, we set foremost in battle.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi bālas taruṇo yuddhānām aviśāradaḥ sadaśva iva saṃbādhe viṣame kṣemam arhati
english: How could a boy, so young, unskilled in the ways of war, win safety in that perilous press, like a fine horse in a treacherous defile?

sanskrit: no ced dhi vayam apy enaṃ mahīm anuśayīmahi bībhatsoḥ kopadīptasya dagdhāḥ kṛpaṇacakṣuṣā
english: Surely we too shall lie down upon the earth beside him, scorched by the pitying glance of Bībhatsu, ablaze with wrath.

sanskrit: alubdho matimān hrīmān kṣamāvān rūpavān balī vapuṣmān mānakṛd vīraḥ priyaḥ satyaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Free of greed, wise, modest, forbearing, handsome, strong, well-formed, honoring others, heroic, beloved, devoted to truth—

sanskrit: yasya ślāghanti vibudhāḥ karmāṇy ūrjitakarmaṇaḥ nivātakavacāñ jaghne kālakeyāṃś ca vīryavān
english: He whose mighty deeds even the gods extol—that valiant one slew the Nivātakavacas and the Kālakeyas.

sanskrit: mahendraśatravo yena hiraṇyapuravāsinaḥ akṣṇor nimeṣamātreṇa paulomāḥ sagaṇā hatāḥ
english: By him the foes of great Indra who dwelt in Hiraṇyapura, the Paulomas with their hosts, were slain in the mere twinkling of an eye.

sanskrit: parebhyo 'py abhayārthibhyo yo dadāty abhayaṃ vibhuḥ tasyāsmābhir na śakitas trātum adyātmajo bhayāt
english: That mighty one who grants safety even to strangers who seek it of him—his own son we have not been able to save this day from peril.

sanskrit: bhayaṃ tu sumahat prāptaṃ dhārtarāṣṭraṃ mahad balam pārthaḥ putravadhāt kruddhaḥ kauravāñ śoṣayiṣyati
english: A most dreadful fear has come upon the great host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son; Pārtha, enraged at the slaying of his son, will wither the Kauravas away.

sanskrit: kṣudraḥ kṣudrasahāyaś ca svapakṣakṣayam āturaḥ vyaktaṃ duryodhano dṛṣṭvā śocan hāsyati jīvitam
english: Mean himself and mean of allies, Duryodhana, beholding in his anguish the ruin of his own faction, will surely grieve and give up his life.

sanskrit: na me jayaḥ prītikaro na rājyaṃ; na cāmaratvaṃ na suraiḥ salokatā imaṃ samīkṣyāprativīryapauruṣaṃ; nipātitaṃ devavarātmajātmajam
english: No victory gladdens me, nor kingdom, nor immortality, nor a place in the world of the gods—seeing him struck down, this matchless one in valor and manhood, the son of the son of the foremost of the gods.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasminn ahani nirvṛtte ghore prāṇabhṛtāṃ kṣaye āditye 'staṃgate śrīmān saṃdhyākāla upasthite
english: Saṃjaya said: When that day had ended in dread destruction of living things, when the sun had set and the glorious hour of twilight had come,

sanskrit: vyapayāteṣu sainyeṣu vāsāya bharatarṣabha hatvā saṃśaptakavrātān divyair astraiḥ kapidhvajaḥ
english: and the armies had departed to their rest, O bull of the Bharatas—having slain the bands of the Saṃśaptakas with celestial weapons, the warrior with the ape upon his banner,

sanskrit: prāyāt svaśibiraṃ jiṣṇur jaitram āsthāya taṃ ratham gacchann eva ca govindaṃ sannakaṇṭho 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Jiṣṇu, mounting that victorious chariot, set out for his own camp; and as he went, with choking voice he spoke to Govinda:

sanskrit: kiṃ nu me hṛdayaṃ trastaṃ vākyaṃ sajjati keśava spandanti cāpy aniṣṭāni gātraṃ sīdati cācyuta
english: Why is my heart so troubled, Keśava, why does my speech falter, why do ill-boding tremors seize me and my limbs grow faint, O Acyuta?

sanskrit: aniṣṭaṃ caiva me śliṣṭaṃ hṛdayān nāpasarpati bhuvi yad dikṣu cāpy ugrā utpātās trāsayanti mām
english: An evil foreboding clings fast and will not depart from my heart; the fierce portents that show upon the earth and in every quarter affright me.

sanskrit: bahuprakārā dṛśyante sarva evāghaśaṃsinaḥ api svasti bhaved rājñaḥ sāmātyasya guror mama
english: Of many kinds they appear, and all forebode calamity. May it yet be well with the king, with his counselors, and with my elders!

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca vyaktaṃ śivaṃ tava bhrātuḥ sāmātyasya bhaviṣyati mā śucaḥ kiṃ cid evānyat tatrāniṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Vāsudeva said: Surely it shall be well with your brother and his counselors. Grieve not; yet some other misfortune there will be.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ saṃdhyām upāsyaiva vīrau vīrāvasādane kathayantau raṇe vṛttaṃ prayātau ratham āsthitau
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, having performed their twilight worship, the two heroes, in their grief for heroes, went on mounted in the chariot, recounting what had befallen in the battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ svaśibiraṃ prāptau hatānandaṃ hatatviṣam vāsudevo 'rjunaś caiva kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram
english: Then Vāsudeva and Arjuna, having wrought a most arduous deed, reached their own camp, now bereft of joy and bereft of splendor.

sanskrit: dhvastākāraṃ samālakṣya śibiraṃ paravīrahā bībhatsur abravīt kṛṣṇam asvasthahṛdayas tataḥ
english: Marking the camp's downcast aspect, Bībhatsu, slayer of hostile heroes, his heart now ill at ease, said to Kṛṣṇa:

sanskrit: nādya nandanti tūryāṇi maṅgalyāni janārdana miśrā dundubhinirghoṣaiḥ śaṅkhāś cāḍambaraiḥ saha vīṇā vā nādya vādyante śamyātālasvanaiḥ saha
english: Today the auspicious instruments raise no joyful sound, Janārdana; no conches mingled with the boom of kettledrums and tabors, nor lutes, are played today with the beat of cymbals and time-keeping clappers.

sanskrit: maṅgalyāni ca gītāni na gāyanti paṭhanti ca stutiyuktāni ramyāṇi mamānīkeṣu bandinaḥ
english: Nor do the bards in my ranks sing or recite the auspicious, lovely songs full of praise.

sanskrit: yodhāś cāpi hi māṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartante hy adhomukhāḥ karmāṇi ca yathāpūrvaṃ kṛtvā nābhivadanti mām
english: And the warriors too, seeing me, turn away with downcast faces, and having done their tasks as before, do not greet me.

sanskrit: api svasti bhaved adya bhrātṛbhyo mama mādhava na hi śudhyati me bhāvo dṛṣṭvā svajanam ākulam
english: May it yet be well today with my brothers, Mādhava; for my mind cannot be eased, seeing my own people in such distress.

sanskrit: api pāñcālarājasya virāṭasya ca mānada sarveṣāṃ caiva yodhānāṃ sāmagryaṃ syān mamācyuta
english: May all be whole, O bestower of honor, with the king of the Pāñcālas and with Virāṭa, and with all my warriors, O Acyuta.

sanskrit: na ca mām adya saubhadraḥ prahṛṣṭo bhrātṛbhiḥ saha raṇād āyāntam ucitaṃ pratyudyāti hasann iva
english: And the son of Subhadrā does not, glad among his brothers as is his wont, come forth smiling to meet me today as I return from battle.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃkathayantau tau praviṣṭau śibiraṃ svakam dadṛśāte bhṛśāsvasthān pāṇḍavān naṣṭacetasaḥ
english: Conversing thus, the two entered their own camp, and beheld the Pāṇḍavas, sorely troubled and stricken out of their senses.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā bhrātṝṃś ca putrāṃś ca vimanā vānaradhvajaḥ apaśyaṃś caiva saubhadram idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing his brothers and his sons, and not seeing the son of Subhadrā, he of the ape-banner, downcast, spoke these words:

sanskrit: mukhavarṇo 'prasanno vaḥ sarveṣām eva lakṣyate na cābhimanyuṃ paśyāmi na ca māṃ pratinandatha
english: The hue of your faces, all of you, is seen to be joyless; I do not see Abhimanyu, nor do you greet me.

sanskrit: mayā śrutaś ca droṇena cakravyūho vinirmitaḥ na ca vas tasya bhettāsti ṛte saubhadram āhave
english: I have heard that Droṇa arrayed the wheel-formation, and that among you there was none to break it in battle save the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: na copadiṣṭas tasyāsīn mayānīkavinirgamaḥ kaccin na bālo yuṣmābhiḥ parānīkaṃ praveśitaḥ
english: But the way out of that array had not been taught to him by me. Surely you did not send the boy into the enemy's host?

sanskrit: bhittvānīkaṃ maheṣvāsaḥ pareṣāṃ bahuśo yudhi kaccin na nihataḥ śete saubhadraḥ paravīrahā
english: Having broken the foes' array again and again in battle, that great archer, the son of Subhadrā, slayer of hostile heroes—surely he does not lie slain?

sanskrit: lohitākṣaṃ mahābāhuṃ jātaṃ siṃham ivādriṣu upendrasadṛśaṃ brūta katham āyodhane hataḥ
english: Red-eyed, mighty-armed, like a lion born among the mountains, like Upendra himself—tell me, how was he slain on the field?

sanskrit: sukumāraṃ maheṣvāsaṃ vāsavasyātmajātmajam sadā mama priyaṃ brūta katham āyodhane hataḥ
english: That tender great archer, the son of the son of Vāsava, ever dear to me—tell me, how was he slain on the field?

sanskrit: vārṣṇeyīdayitaṃ śūraṃ mayā satatalālitam ambāyāś ca priyaṃ nityaṃ ko 'vadhīt kālacoditaḥ
english: That hero, beloved of the Vārṣṇeya woman, ever cherished by me, ever dear to his mother—who, driven by fate, has slain him?

sanskrit: sadṛśo vṛṣṇisiṃhasya keśavasya mahātmanaḥ vikramaśrutamāhātmyaiḥ katham āyodhane hataḥ
english: In valor, in fame, in greatness of soul the equal of the lion of the Vṛṣṇis, the high-souled Keśava—how was he slain on the field?

sanskrit: subhadrāyāḥ priyaṃ nityaṃ draupadyāḥ keśavasya ca yadi putraṃ na paśyāmi yāsyāmi yamasādanam
english: Ever dear to Subhadrā, to Draupadī, and to Keśava—if I do not see my son, I shall go to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: mṛdukuñcitakeśāntaṃ bālaṃ bālamṛgekṣaṇam mattadviradavikrāntaṃ śālapotam ivodgatam
english: With soft, curling hair, a youth with the eyes of a young fawn, striding like a maddened elephant, sprung up like a young śāla tree—

sanskrit: smitābhibhāṣiṇaṃ dāntaṃ guruvākyakaraṃ sadā bālye 'py abālakarmāṇaṃ priyavākyam amatsaram
english: Speaking with a smile, self-controlled, ever obedient to his elders' word, even in boyhood doing no boyish deeds, sweet of speech and without envy—

sanskrit: mahotsāhaṃ mahābāhuṃ dīrgharājīvalocanam bhaktānukampinaṃ dāntaṃ na ca nīcānusāriṇam
english: Of great resolve, mighty-armed, with long lotus-petal eyes, compassionate to those devoted to him, self-restrained, and following nothing base—

sanskrit: kṛtajñaṃ jñānasaṃpannaṃ kṛtāstram anivartinam yuddhābhinandinaṃ nityaṃ dviṣatām aghavardhanam
english: Grateful, endowed with knowledge, skilled in arms, never turning back, ever delighting in battle, increaser of his foes' woe—

sanskrit: sveṣāṃ priyahite yuktaṃ pitṝṇāṃ jayagṛddhinam na ca pūrvaprahartāraṃ saṃgrāme naṣṭasaṃbhramam yadi putraṃ na paśyāmi yāsyāmi yamasādanam
english: Devoted to the welfare of his own, eager for his fathers' victory, never the first to strike, unflustered in battle—if I do not see my son, I shall go to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: sulalāṭaṃ sukeśāntaṃ subhrvakṣidaśanacchadam apaśyatas tad vadanaṃ kā śāntir hṛdayasya me
english: His fair brow, his fair hair, his lovely eyebrows, eyes, and lips—if I see not that face, what peace can there be for my heart?

sanskrit: tantrīsvanasukhaṃ ramyaṃ puṃskokilasamadhvanim aśṛṇvataḥ svanaṃ tasya kā śāntir hṛdayasya me
english: His voice, sweet as the sound of strings, lovely, melodious as the male cuckoo's note—if I hear not that voice, what peace can there be for my heart?

sanskrit: rūpaṃ cāpratirūpaṃ tat tridaśeṣv api durlabham apaśyato 'dya vīrasya kā śāntir hṛdayasya me
english: That beauty without compare, hard to find even among the gods—if I see not the hero's beauty this day, what peace can there be for my heart?

sanskrit: abhivādanadakṣaṃ taṃ pitṝṇāṃ vacane ratam nādyāhaṃ yadi paśyāmi kā śāntir hṛdayasya me
english: Skilled in courteous salutation, devoted to the word of his elders—if I do not see him this day, what peace can there be for my heart?

sanskrit: sukumāraḥ sadā vīro mahārhaśayanocitaḥ bhūmāv anāthavac chete nūnaṃ nāthavatāṃ varaḥ
english: That tender hero, ever fit for the most precious couch—he, surely the best of those who have protectors, now lies upon the bare earth like one forlorn.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ samupāsanti yaṃ purā paramastriyaḥ tam adya vipraviddhāṅgam upāsanty aśivāḥ śivāḥ
english: He whom of old the loveliest women attended as he lay—him today, his limbs flung wide, the inauspicious she-jackals attend.

sanskrit: yaḥ purā bodhyate suptaḥ sūtamāgadhabandibhiḥ bodhayanty adya taṃ nūnaṃ śvāpadā vikṛtaiḥ svaraiḥ
english: He whom of old, when he slept, the bards, heralds, and panegyrists awakened—him today, surely, the beasts of prey awaken with their hideous cries.

sanskrit: chatracchāyāsamucitaṃ tasya tad vadanaṃ śubham nūnam adya rajodhvastaṃ raṇe reṇuḥ kariṣyati
english: That fair face of his, accustomed to the shade of the parasol, the dust of battle will surely cover this day with grime.

sanskrit: hā putrakāvitṛptasya satataṃ putradarśane bhāgyahīnasya kālena yathā me nīyase balāt
english: Alas, my little son! How, by the working of time, are you torn by force from me—luckless, and never sated with the sight of my son!

sanskrit: sādya saṃyamanī nūnaṃ sadā sukṛtināṃ gatiḥ svabhābhir bhāsitā ramyā tvayātyarthaṃ virājate
english: Surely the city of restraint, the ever-lovely goal of the virtuous, lit by your own radiance, shines this day exceedingly because of you.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ vaivasvataś ca tvā varuṇaś ca priyātithiḥ śatakratur dhaneśaś ca prāptam arcanty abhīrukam
english: Surely Vaivasvata and Varuṇa, fond of guests, and Śatakratu and the lord of wealth honor you, the fearless one, now that you have come to them.

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapya bahudhā bhinnapoto vaṇig yathā duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭo yudhiṣṭhiram apṛcchata
english: Having lamented thus in many ways, like a merchant whose ship is wrecked, overwhelmed by great grief, he questioned Yudhiṣṭhira:

sanskrit: kaccit sa kadanaṃ kṛtvā pareṣāṃ pāṇḍunandana svargato 'bhimukhaḥ saṃkhye yudhyamāno nararṣabhaḥ
english: Tell me, O son of Pāṇḍu, did that bull among men, having wrought havoc among the foes, go to heaven facing them, fighting in the battle?

sanskrit: sa nūnaṃ bahubhir yattair yudhyamāno nararṣabhaiḥ asahāyaḥ sahāyārthī mām anudhyātavān dhruvam
english: Surely, fighting against many straining bulls among men, helpless and craving a helper, he thought of me, of that I am certain.

sanskrit: pīḍyamānaḥ śarair bālas tāta sādhv abhidhāva mām iti vipralapan manye nṛśaṃsair bahubhir hataḥ
english: Tormented by arrows, the boy crying out, 'Father, come quickly to my aid!'—thus lamenting, I think, he was slain by many cruel men.

sanskrit: atha vā matprasūtaś ca svasrīyo mādhavasya ca subhadrāyāṃ ca saṃbhūto naivaṃ vaktum ihārhati
english: Yet, born of me, the sister's son of Mādhava too, sprung from Subhadrā—he is not one to speak so.

sanskrit: vajrasāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ mama apaśyato dīrghabāhuṃ raktākṣaṃ yan na dīryate
english: Surely my heart is made of the very stuff of adamant, so hard that it does not burst, though I see not that long-armed, red-eyed one.

sanskrit: kathaṃ bāle maheṣvāse nṛśaṃsā marmabhedinaḥ svasrīye vāsudevasya mama putre 'kṣipañ śarān
english: How could those cruel men loose their vital-piercing arrows upon a boy, a great archer, the sister's son of Vāsudeva, my own son?

sanskrit: yo māṃ nityam adīnātmā pratyudgamyābhinandati upayāntaṃ ripūn hatvā so 'dya māṃ kiṃ na paśyati
english: He who, never downcast in spirit, would ever come forth to greet me with joy as I drew near from slaying the foe—why does he not look upon me today?

sanskrit: nūnaṃ sa patitaḥ śete dharaṇyāṃ rudhirokṣitaḥ śobhayan medinīṃ gātrair āditya iva pātitaḥ
english: Surely he lies fallen upon the earth, drenched in blood, gracing the ground with his limbs, like the sun cast down.
